title: Birthday Problem: Threshold for 99% Match Probability

problemStatement.plain: In a group of 57 people (with 365 equally likely birthdays), the probability of at least two sharing a birthday exceeds 99%. With 56 people, it is still below 99%. So 57 is the exact threshold.
whyMatters: Natural extension of the birthday problem beyond the 50% threshold
Demonstrates that the birthday paradox becomes overwhelming quickly
The jump from 50% (n=23) to 99% (n=57) shows sublinear growth of threshold

knownResults.goal: Complete: prove 57 is exact threshold for 99% birthday match probability

currentState.focus: Proved both directions of the 99% threshold: P(57) > 99/100 and P(56) < 99/100.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: 2 new theorems added to BirthdayProblem.lean. The 99% threshold is n=57, proved via native_decide on large integer inequalities (365^57 vs 100*descFactorial(365,57)).
insights: Same proof pattern as the 50% threshold: reduce to integer inequality, verify with native_decide
The 99% threshold (57) is surprisingly close to the 50% threshold (23) - only 2.5x more people

approaches.name: Integer inequality via native_decide
approaches.description: Reduce probability inequality to integer comparison 100*descFactorial(365,n) vs 365^n, verify with native_decide
